 Kids' bike helmets sold at Dick's, JC Penny recalled over risk of serious injury, death 
 Parents of kids with the bike helmets should make sure they stop using them "immediately," according to the recall. 
 By Izzy Stroobandt • 
 Published November 19, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 19, 2026 at 9:24 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 You’re watching the NBC 5 Chicago News streaming channel, which plays local Chicago news 24 hours a day, seven days a week. You can find the “NBC 5 Chicago News” streaming channel on your phone or computer, and on Peacock, Samsung, Roku, Xumo or on our app, so you can watch our local news on your schedule.
 Thousands of kids' bike helmets sold at popular retailers were recalled Thursday because they violate mandatory standards and pose a risk of serious injury or death, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. 
 Cipton issued a recall of nearly 17,000 of its bike helmets because they "violate the mandatory safety standard for bicycle helmets" and "do not comply with the impact attenuation, positional stability and certification requirements," the recall alert states .

 In the event of a crash, the helmets can fail to protect a child's head and pose a serious risk of injury or death, according to USCPSC.
 The recalled helmets were sold in white and in youth size small at Dick's Sporting Goods and JC Penny stores nationwide and online at Dickssportinggoods.com from April 2024 through May 2026 for roughly $35.
 A label on the inside of the recalled helmets will have model “CPSK300CC” is printed on it, according to the recall alert. They also have black padding, black straps, black buckle and a built-in, multi-colored LED light strip. 
 "Consumers should stop using the helmets immediately and contact Cipton for a full refund. Consumers will be asked to destroy the helmet by cutting the straps and writing in permanent marker 'Recalled' on the helmet and send a photo of the destroyed helmet to Reply@customersupport123.com. Consumers should then dispose of the recalled product," the recall alert says. Because of the lithium-ion battery in the helmet's lights, it's important to properly dispose of the helmet.
 The recall comes one day after Illinois officials also warned parents to be weary of the kind of e-bikes they purchase their kids for Christmas or risk facing consequences as new legislation goes into effect on Jan. 1.
